My 2 recommendations:

  • Frank Herbert - Dune series
  • Isaac Asimov - Foundation series, and them maybe Robot series

Both made a profound impact on the whole Sci-Fi genre.

Dune is my favourite scifi series (so I'm not objective). Pretty much everyone that the first book (Dune) is great. Then, there are 2 interesting books which introduce a more philosophical side of series Dune Messiah and Children of Dune. Some don't enjoy them very much, but they're a good introduction to the 4th book - by many Dune fans (myself included) the best book of series - God Emperor Of Dune. Then they're followed by 2 last books of the series - which are good, but quite strange, and unlike the rest of the series.

Regarding Asimov - almost all his books are good reads. I don't find the Foundation as profound as Dune, but it's very well written and consistent. The Robot stories introduce more interesting ideas, since I'm a programmer some of his observations resonate quite well with me. I often find them even mind-blowing, when I realize that those (still very relevant, or even more relevant now) stories were written in 50s or 60s.

I'm a fantasy reader and am also reading the Stormlight Archives, and very much enjoying the story so far. Some other fantasy authors that I read / have read are:

Raymond E Feist - starting with 'Magician' and then on through the whole Midkemia series of stories. He invented his world(s) and then wrote several series through generations of families / characters. All excellent reads.

David Gemmell - Starting with Legend. I love David for his ability to get a complete fantasy story into a 200 - 300 page book, and he has created some brilliant, complex characters.

Obviously as you know of Brandon Sanderson you may well be aware of the Wheel of Time series that he finished writing for Robert Jordan after Robert's death. It's a fourteen book story, all books are 600 - 1000 pages long. It kinda gets bogged down a little in the middle, but the first in the series was the first book that my dad lent me when I was about 13 and fully sparked my love of reading, and reading fantasy in particular.

I've also enjoyed the Song of Ice and Fire books recently. If you're familiar with the Game of Thrones TV series at all then it's definitely worth reading the books.

Good luck, and let me know if you find anything good!

The Shadow of What Was Lost by James Islington. I'm about halfway through and I'm really enjoying it. It's apparently the first book in a planned trilogy.

The World at the End of Time by Frederik Pohl. I absolutely loved this book, scifi. Very clever stuff.
